case_studies.title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
case_studies.abstract: Real-time multimodal applications, including voice agents and interactive video generation, compose heterogeneous models into pipelines whose efficient deployment requires application-specific decisions about placement, streaming, and intra-model parallelism. Existing serving systems and auto-parallelism compilers commit to limited transformations and fixed workload assumptions, so achieving high performance on a new application requires hand-crafting an efficient implementation. We present FlashRT, an agent harness that guides coding agents to lift simple developer-written reference implement
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of efficiently deploying real-time multimodal applications by building FlashRT, an agent harness that guides coding agents to optimize application deployment. The result is a more efficient and automated way to deploy complex applications. This technology has the potential to simplify the deployment of real-time applications in cloud environments.

case_studies.title: HyMCache: A KV Cache Framework for Multi-Turn LLM Serving with CXL-Hybrid Memory
case_studies.abstract: Long-context, multi-turn, and agentic LLM workloads increasingly reuse previously processed context, making KV-cache reuse essential for reducing redundant computation. However, this reuse shifts the bottleneck to the memory tier that stores and serves reusable KV states at cluster scale. GPU HBM and host DRAM are too costly to scale to TB-scale shared context capacity, motivating remote tiers built from lower-cost, higher-capacity media. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of efficient memory use for large language models by building a framework called HyMCache, which integrates CXL-hybrid memory to reduce redundant computation. The result is a more scalable and cost-effective way to store and serve reusable data. This could improve the performance of cloud-based language processing applications.

In smart grids, recent work applies agentic schemes to forecasting, optimization, and control, wrapping trusted solvers behind language interfaces and orchestrating multi-step workflows. case_studies.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
case_studies.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) on open-ended tasks compresses an LLM's rubric-based evaluation into a scalar reward, discarding rich textual feedback and conflating responses with distinct quality profiles. We propose Experiential Learning (EL), which repurposes the feedback model from an LLM-as-a-Judge into an LLM-as-a-Coach. The coach distills its assessment of each on-policy response into transferable experiential knowledge, which conditions a teacher model and is internalized by the policy through on-policy context distillation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited feedback in reinforcement learning tasks by building a coaching model that provides richer feedback, resulting in improved learning outcomes. The researchers built an Experiential Learning model that repurposes a large language model as a coach, providing more detailed feedback to learners. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.abstract: Rubric-based RL has recently shown promise in improving LLMs on open-ended tasks. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited exploration in rubric-based reinforcement learning by building a self-distillation method, resulting in improved optimization of language models. case_studies.title: Stress Testing Concept Erasure with Large Language Model Agents
case_studies.abstract: Concept erasure aims to remove semantic concepts from a trained generative model and is increasingly important for responsible AI deployment. However, verifying whether a model has robustly removed targeted concepts remains a critical challenge. case_studies.title: An Explicit World Model Based on Data-First Ontology: DaoQL Multimodal Storage Validation and Counterfactual Reasoning Evaluation
case_studies.abstract: Large language models encode world models implicitly in neural weights, which exposes four structural risks in high-precision domains such as medicine and finance: hallucination, frozen knowledge, poor explainability, and poor modifiability. This paper proposes data-first ontology: LLMs are treated as reasoning and language engines, while deterministic knowledge is moved into an explicit multimodal database, DaoQL. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models having implicit world models that can lead to hallucination, frozen knowledge, and poor explainability. The authors built a data-first ontology called DaoQL, which moves deterministic knowledge into an explicit multimodal database. The result shows that explicit models provide a sufficient condition for reliable evaluation and reasoning.

case_studies.title: GARAGE: Characterizing the Automation Boundary in LLM-based Attack Graph Generation
case_studies.abstract: While modern vehicle security depends on effective Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) synthesis, current automated tools struggle with unstructured data and automotive-specific architectural nuances. To bridge this gap, we introduce GARAGE, a RAG-powered framework that converts fragmented CTI into an actionable, domain-specific knowledge base for automated attack graph generation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automating cyber threat intelligence for vehicle security by building a framework called GARAGE, which converts fragmented data into an actionable knowledge base, resulting in a comprehensive dataset of known vulnerabilities and incidents. The framework generates attack graphs to help predict potential threats. This research is mainly related to automotive cyber security.
